Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon), a VPS/game hosting business. Build TWO related but distinct discount features, both already researched (context below is from a completed read-only investigation — trust it, don't re-derive from scratch, but DO verify specifics by reading the actual files before writing code).

## FEATURE 1: Exit-intent popup, 25% off, first-time customers only, on the deploy wizard's pricing step

**Trigger**: a signed-in user who has never purchased anything (zero non-free `Server` rows: `db.server.count({ where: { userId, isFree: false } }) === 0` — this is the codebase's own established "first-time customer" predicate, already used identically in `lib/order.ts:574,620` and `lib/coupon-redemption.ts:174` for `firstTimeOnly` coupon enforcement) reaches the deploy wizard's pricing step — VPS: `id="s-configure"` ("Choose your plan"), game: `id="s-gconf"` ("Size your server"), both in `components/nx/DeployView.tsx` — and shows exit intent (mouse moving toward the top of the viewport / browser chrome, the classic exit-intent pattern: `document.addEventListener("mouseleave", e => { if (e.clientY <= 0) ... })`, or attempting to navigate away). No exit-intent detection exists anywhere in this codebase today — this is genuinely new.

**Popup**: real Nxeon-branded modal (not a generic browser confirm/alert) saying something like "You're almost there — here's 25% off, limited time" with a "Claim now" action. Copy should feel urgent but not sleazy; use your judgment on exact wording, keep it short.

**Mechanism — reuse the REAL coupon engine, don't build a parallel one**:
- Create a real `Coupon` row (via a migration/seed script, or `adminCreateCoupon` in `lib/actions-growth.ts` if that's easily scriptable — check it first): `code: "EXIT25"`, `kind: "PERCENT"`, `value: 25`, `scope: "ANY"`, `firstTimeOnly: true`, `active: true`, no `maxRedemptions` cap needed (the `firstTimeOnly` + per-user unique-redemption constraint already prevents abuse) — but DO set a reasonable `maxTermMonths` if that field exists and other real coupons in this DB commonly set one, to avoid a runaway multi-year 25%-off if someone buys a 3-year term (check how `lib/coupon-order.ts` and existing seeded coupons handle this, follow the same convention).
- "Claim now" should apply this coupon code to the IN-PROGRESS order the same way manually typing a coupon code into the wizard's promo-code field already does (there's a `couponCode` field the wizard already has — reuse that exact application path, e.g. autofill it and trigger the existing validation/apply flow, or call whatever the wizard's existing "apply coupon" handler is, rather than inventing a second code path). If the wizard doesn't currently show its promo-code field until later in the flow, make "Claim now" fill it in and reveal it / show the discount applied inline as confirmation.
- Only show ONCE per session/visit (don't re-trigger every time the mouse leaves) — use component state, not persistent storage, unless you have a reason to persist across a reload (use your judgment, document why).
- Do NOT show to a user who already has a real Server (not first-time) — check eligibility server-side (the deploy page is already a server component reading `user` — thread a boolean prop down, don't trust a client-only check for something this consequential).

## FEATURE 2: Cancel-plan / delete-account retention offer, 50% off

**Trigger**: when a customer attempts to cancel a server's auto-renewal ("cancel plan" / "don't renew") OR attempts to delete their account — find these actual flows in the dashboard first (search `app/dashboard/` and `components/customer/`/`components/nx/` for the real cancel-renewal and delete-account actions/UI — likely `lib/actions.ts` or `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts` for server cancellation, and wherever account deletion lives, e.g. `lib/actions-account.ts` or similar — READ the real code before assuming the shape).

**This is fundamentally different from Feature 1** — it can't reuse the checkout-time `Coupon`/order-quote stacking logic (`lib/order.ts`/`lib/game-order.ts`), because there's no new order happening; the discount needs to apply to a FUTURE RENEWAL CHARGE on an EXISTING server. This means touching `lib/renewal-charge.ts` (the same file modified carefully in the recent "grandfather pricing program" work — read its current state and doc comments in full before touching it) and/or `worker/billing.ts` (the actual recurring-charge worker).

**Design this carefully, following the EXACT precedent already in this codebase for "a stored per-server override read by `renewalCharge()`"** — `Server.grandfatheredRenewalCents` is the existing pattern for "a frozen value that overrides the live catalog price at renewal time." For a ONE-TIME, TEMPORARY discount (not permanent), you likely need a similar but distinct field — e.g. `Server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent Int?` (or similar name matching this codebase's naming conventions) that `renewalCharge()` applies ONCE on the very next renewal, then the worker clears it after that renewal actually happens (so it's not accidentally reapplied every renewal forever). Think through and handle: what if the customer cancels again after redeeming once (must not be re-offerable — use the SAME single coupon-like mechanism, e.g. a real `Coupon` row `code: "STAY50", kind: PERCENT, value: 50` with `maxRedemptions` per-user enforced via the existing `CouponRedemption` unique-per-(coupon,user) constraint — reuse the general coupon engine for ELIGIBILITY/one-time-redemption bookkeeping even though the actual discount APPLICATION mechanism has to be the new renewal-time field, since the checkout-order coupon-stacking code path doesn't fire here at all). What happens if they cancel a DIFFERENT server later — should the SAME account be offerable again for a different server? Use your judgment, document the reasoning, and add real tests (following this codebase's existing test-writing convention in `test/money-core-guards.test.ts` — read a few existing tests there for the exact style/rigor bar before writing new ones) proving: (a) the discount actually reduces the very next renewal charge by 50%, (b) it does NOT apply to the renewal after that, (c) a customer who already redeemed it once cannot get it offered/applied again.

**Popup/modal**: shown as an interstitial when they click cancel/delete, before the action actually completes — "Wait — before you go, here's 50% off your next renewal. Stay and save?" with options to accept (claims the discount, does NOT cancel) or continue with the cancellation/deletion anyway. Don't make it deceptive or hard to decline — a clear, real choice, not a dark pattern that traps them.

## BOTH FEATURES — shared conventions
- Add a lightweight admin on/off toggle for each, following the exact shape of the existing `WinbackPanel.tsx` / `lib/actions-settings.ts` pattern (a new settings section, e.g. `"exit_intent"` and `"retention_offer"`, each with at least an `_enabled` boolean, default true since the owner explicitly asked for these to be live now — check `lib/settings.ts` for how existing sections declare their keys/defaults and follow that exactly).
- Test in an actual browser for Feature 1 (trigger the exit-intent, confirm the modal appears once, confirm claiming it actually reduces the displayed price) — check CLAUDE.md's build-isolation rule, don't build directly in /opt/nxeon.
- Feature 2 needs real backend tests (per above) since a live browser click-test can't itself prove the renewal-charge math is correct weeks later — the automated test suite is the real verification here, run it and show it passing.
- Credential hygiene: any DB read/write via a `.ts` script under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db`, run via `npx tsx` from `/opt/nxeon` — never construct/print a raw `psql`/`DATABASE_URL` connection string (this has leaked the production DB password into logs twice already this session).
- Deploy through the normal pipeline: commit → push → deploy-staging.sh → verify HTTP 200 → promote-production.sh → verify HTTP 200 AND a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID (compare against current value first). Other background work may be concurrently touching this repo/deploy pipeline (a marketing-pricing sweep is running in parallel) — if a deploy collides, retry once after confirming staging is still healthy; don't revert someone else's in-flight work.

Report back concisely: exact files changed for each feature, the real Coupon rows created (code/kind/value/flags), the new `Server`/schema field added for Feature 2 and exactly how `renewalCharge()`/the billing worker now uses and clears it, your test results (both the browser check for Feature 1 and the automated test names/pass-status for Feature 2), and confirmation of production deploy with a fresh BUILD_ID.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.
17	
18	- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
19	  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
20	  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
21	  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).
22	
23	- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
24	  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
25	  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
26	  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).
27	
28	- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
29	  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
30	  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
31	  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
32	  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
33	  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
34	  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
35	  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.
36	
37	- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
38	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
39	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).
40	
41	## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session
42	
43	`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.
44	
45	1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
46	2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
47	3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
48	4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
49	5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.
50	
51	If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).
52	
53	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
54	
55	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
56	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
57	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
58	
59	## Conventions
60	
61	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
62	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
63	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
64	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
65	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
66	- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
67	- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.
68	
69	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
70	
71	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
72	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
73	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
74	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
75	
76	## Commands
77	
78	- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
79	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
80	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
81	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
82	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
83	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
84	
85	## Domains & TLS
86	
87	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
88	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
89	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
90	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
91	
92	## Environments
93	
94	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
95	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
96	- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
97	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
98	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.
99	
100	## Safety rules
101	
102	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
103	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
104	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
105	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
106	- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
107	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
108	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
109

9	// that has never been written falls back to its SETTINGS_DEFAULTS value. Booleans

595	/** True-ish coercion for values stored as "true"/"false"/"on"/"1". */
596	export function isTrue(v: string | undefined | null): boolean {
597	  return v === "true" || v === "on" || v === "1";
598	}

600	/** Read one setting, falling back to an explicit default then SETTINGS_DEFAULTS. */
601	export async function getSetting(key: SettingKey | string, fallback?: string): Promise<string> {
602	  const row = await db.setting.findUnique({ where: { key } });
603	  if (row) return row.value;
604	  return fallback ?? SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[key as SettingKey] ?? "";
605	}
606	
607	/** Read one setting as a boolean. */
608	export async function getSettingBool(key: SettingKey | string, fallback = false): Promise<boolean> {
609	  const row = await db.setting.findUnique({ where: { key } });
610	  if (row) return isTrue(row.value);
611	  const def = SETTINGS_DEFAULTS[key as SettingKey];
612	  return def !== undefined ? isTrue(def) : fallback;
613	}
614	
615	/** Read one setting as an integer (cents, days, counts…). */
616	export async function getSettingInt(key: SettingKey | string, fallback = 0): Promise<number> {
617	  const raw = await getSetting(key, String(fallback));
618	  const n = Number(raw);
619	  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : fallback;
620	}

623	export async function setSetting(key: SettingKey | string, value: string): Promise<void> {
624	  await db.setting.upsert({
625	    where: { key },
626	    update: { value },
627	    create: { key, value },
628	  });
629	}

633	 * ARE included — callers that hand this to the client (the settings page) must
634	 * strip SECRET_KEYS themselves.

636	export async function getAllSettings(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
637	  const rows = await db.setting.findMany();

645	 * platform can actually sell.
646	 *
647	 * The guarantee is the point. `default_term` was previously the enum
648	 * "monthly"|"quarterly"|"annual" and the platform's real terms are 1/12/24/36 months
649	 * (`VPS_TERMS`) — "quarterly" mapped to nothing at all. Anything stored that
650	 * `VPS_TERMS` does not contain (a legacy row, or a hand-crafted POST that slipped past
651	 * the panel's enum check) falls back to the first term rather than pre-selecting a
652	 * commitment no charge path can price. A wizard that pre-selects an unsellable term
653	 * would fail at `vpsTerm()`'s own silent `?? VPS_TERMS[0]` fallback, charging monthly
654	 * while the review step displayed something else.

657	  const months = Number(await getSetting("default_term"));
658	  return VPS_TERMS.some((t) => t.months === months) ? months : VPS_TERMS[0].months;

1	import { vpsTerm, vpsTermPriceCents, termPriceCents } from "./billing-terms";
2	import { extraDiskCentsAt } from "./extra-disk";
3	import { type BackupTier, backupTierMonthlyCents } from "./backup-tiers";
4	
5	/**
6	 * What one renewal costs — the SINGLE definition, used by every path that quotes
7	 * or charges one: the automatic sweep in worker/billing.ts, the saved-card path,
8	 * the "Renew now" button, the server page and the deploy wizard's term cards.
9	 *
10	 * WHY IT LIVES IN ITS OWN FILE. It used to sit in lib/stripe-cards.ts, which
11	 * imports the Stripe SDK and (transitively) nodemailer. The moment a CLIENT
12	 * component — the deploy wizard — needed the renewal price, that import chain
13	 * dragged `nodemailer/lib/dkim` into the browser bundle and the build failed with
14	 * "Can't resolve 'fs'". The pricing rule is pure arithmetic and has no business
15	 * carrying a mail transport with it, so it lives here with only the two tiny
16	 * modules it genuinely needs. lib/stripe-cards.ts re-exports it, so no server-side
17	 * caller had to change.
18	 *
19	 * The rule this file exists to enforce: there is ONE renewal formula. Two
20	 * incidents in one day came from a second copy — first a button that hardcoded
21	 * "+30 days" and the monthly price while the action charged a full term ($8.99
22	 * shown, $97.09 taken), then the shared quote written to fix it, which computed
23	 * from `plan.priceCents` and so ignored `gamePlan` and would have billed a $4.99
24	 * game server at its $8.99 base plan. Do not add a second formula.
25	 */
26	export type RenewalCharge = {
27	  months: number;
28	  /**
29	   * The amount to CHARGE / display — tax-INCLUSIVE (net + tax). When no
30	   * `taxRatePercent` is supplied (the default), tax is 0 and this equals `netCents`,
31	   * so every existing caller is unchanged. Because display and charge both read this
32	   * one field, `displayed === charged === renewed` holds by construction.
33	   */
34	  totalCents: number;
35	  /** The pre-tax subtotal (plan + IP + disk + backup). Invoice line items sum to this. */
36	  netCents: number;
37	  /** The VAT/GST added on top of `netCents` (Finding 1); 0 when no rate was passed. */
38	  taxCents: number;
39	  /** The rate (%) `taxCents` was computed at, recorded on the invoice. */
40	  taxRatePercent: number;
41	  /** The extra-root-disk portion, which gets its own invoice line. */
42	  extraDiskCents: number;
43	  extraDiskMonthlyCents: number;
44	  /** The paid backup-tier portion (Plus retention), which gets its own invoice line. */
45	  backupCents: number;
46	  backupMonthlyCents: number;
47	  /** Human label for the invoice / receipt ("Nebula VPS" or the game plan name). */
48	  label: string;
49	};
50	
51	export type PricedServer = {
52	  termMonths: number;
53	  extraDiskGB: number;
54	  plan: { name: string; priceCents: number };
55	  gamePlan: { name: string; priceCents: number; termMonths: number } | null;
56	  dedicatedIp: unknown | null;
57	  /**
58	   * Did the customer actually choose/pay for this IP, vs. a VPS just being
59	   * handed one for free by the `dedicated_ip_default` platform setting? See the
60	   * IP surcharge lines below for why this has to gate the charge alongside
61	   * `dedicatedIp` itself.
62	   */
63	  wantsDedicatedIp: boolean;
64	  /** Paid backup retention tier. A full Server row supplies it; synthetic callers must pass it. */
65	  backupTier: BackupTier;
66	  /**
67	   * The ANNUAL discount FROZEN on this server at sale (`Server.annualDiscountPct`),
68	   * or null on a legacy/monthly/flat row. OPTIONAL so the many synthetic
69	   * `PricedServer` display/quote objects keep compiling; a full Server row supplies
70	   * it automatically. When present it WINS over the live `prices.annualDiscountPct`,
71	   * so an annual VPS / NxCloud / game server renews at exactly the rate it was
72	   * SOLD at even if the admin retunes the setting afterwards; null falls back to
73	   * the live rate, which for every non-annual term is identical maths.
74	   */
75	  annualDiscountPct?: number | null;
76	  /**
77	   * GRANDFATHER PROGRAM (2026-09-17): the plan/game-plan monthly rate FROZEN
78	   * on this server at sale (`Server.grandfatheredRenewalCents`), read here
79	   * INSTEAD OF the live `plan.priceCents` / `gamePlan.priceCents` when
80	   * present. OPTIONAL, same shape as `annualDiscountPct` above — every
81	   * existing synthetic `PricedServer` (wizard previews, tests) keeps
82	   * compiling and keeps pricing off the live catalog rate exactly as
83	   * before; only a real Server row (which supplies it automatically)
84	   * actually grandfathers anything. Null/undefined = price off the live
85	   * plan, which is correct for a legacy pre-program row that was never
86	   * backfilled AND for a free/admin server with no real price to freeze.
87	   */
88	  grandfatheredRenewalCents?: number | null;
89	};
90	
91	/**
92	 * The admin-priced inputs a renewal is charged against. Every field is REQUIRED
93	 * deliberately, mirroring how the codebase guards renewal pricing everywhere else
94	 * (`termPromoPercent` is likewise required in lib/proration.ts): a call site that
95	 * builds this object cannot silently forget one and fall back to a stale default.
96	 */
97	export type RenewalPrices = {
98	  ipMonthlyCents: number;
99	  extraDiskPerGbCents: number;
100	  backupPlusCents: number;
101	  /**
102	   * The admin-configured ANNUAL discount (percent), resolved from the
103	   * `annual_discount_percent` setting via `annualDiscountPct()`.
104	   *
105	   * REQUIRED — not optional. A 12-month server renews at
106	   * `vpsTermPriceCents(price, 12, annualDiscountPct)`; if a call site could OMIT
107	   * this it would silently price annual at the shipped default (10%) while the
108	   * owner had set, say, 20% — the rate the customer was shown and charged at order.
109	   * Required turns that into a compile error at every one of the ~8 places that
110	   * build this object, so the annual setting cannot be forgotten on any renewal
111	   * path and `displayed === charged === renewed` holds.
112	   */
113	  annualDiscountPct: number;
114	  /**
115	   * OPTIONAL destination VAT/GST rate (percent) for the customer who owns this
116	   * server, resolved from their billing country (lib/tax.ts taxContextForUser).
117	   * Omitted / 0 => no tax added and `totalCents === netCents`, so every call site
118	   * that does not opt in is byte-for-byte unchanged. A charge site passes the
119	   * OWNER's rate so the wallet debit, the card leg and the invoice all agree; a
120	   * display of the owner's own renewal passes the SAME rate so the figure shown
121	   * equals the figure taken.
122	   */
123	  taxRatePercent?: number;
124	};
125	
126	export function renewalCharge(
127	  server: PricedServer,
128	  prices: RenewalPrices,
129	): RenewalCharge {
130	  const isGame = !!server.gamePlan;
131	  // The term to renew — the customer's chosen `Server.termMonths` (1 = monthly,
132	  // 12 = annual). A game term is now a per-order choice (Monthly / Annual) just like
133	  // a VPS, so it rides the Server row, not the plan.
134	  //
135	  // VPS/NxCloud terms are always one of the 4 standard `VPS_TERMS`, so we normalise
136	  // through `vpsTerm`. A GAME server, however, may historically carry ANY term the
137	  // plan was configured with (a pre-existing game server was created with
138	  // `termMonths = gamePlan.termMonths`, which the admin can set 1..36). We therefore
139	  // read the game term back RAW (clamped >= 1) rather than through `vpsTerm`, whose
140	  // fallback would collapse a non-standard legacy value (say 3) to monthly and
141	  // change that server's renewal cadence. For the seeded games (all `termMonths: 1`)
142	  // and any new Monthly/Annual order this is identical to the standard path.
143	  const months = isGame ? Math.max(1, Math.round(server.termMonths)) : vpsTerm(server.termMonths).months;
144	  // The annual discount to price the term at: the rate FROZEN on the server at sale,
145	  // falling back to the live setting for legacy/monthly rows. Both halves resolve
146	  // the same number, so an annual sub renews at the sold rate.
147	  const annualPct = server.annualDiscountPct ?? prices.annualDiscountPct;
148	  // Extra root disk is billed EVERY cycle at the current per-GB price. Game plans
149	  // are a flat all-in price and never carry the add-on lines.
150	  const extraDiskMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : extraDiskCentsAt(server.extraDiskGB, prices.extraDiskPerGbCents);
151	  const extraDiskCents = extraDiskMonthlyCents * months;
152	  // Paid backup retention (Plus) rides alongside extra disk: billed every cycle at
153	  // the current admin price, and — like every add-on line — NOT carried by a game
154	  // plan (renewalCharge's game branch is flat all-in, so game servers are never
155	  // sold a paid backup tier; see lib/backup-upgrade.ts's game guard).
156	  const backupMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : backupTierMonthlyCents(server.backupTier, prices.backupPlusCents);
157	  const backupCents = backupMonthlyCents * months;
158	  // GRANDFATHER PROGRAM: the frozen rate wins over the live catalog price when
159	  // set (see PricedServer.grandfatheredRenewalCents's own doc comment) — this
160	  // is the ONE substitution point for both branches below, so a price rise on
161	  // the live Plan/GamePlan row never touches a server that already has a
162	  // frozen rate, while every other renewal-formula behavior (term math, annual
163	  // discount, add-ons) is completely unchanged.
164	  const grandfatheredPriceCents = server.grandfatheredRenewalCents ?? null;
165	  // A game plan's `priceCents` is its MONTHLY base (every seed is `termMonths: 1`).
166	  // Divide by the plan's own term so an admin plan configured as, say, a 3-month
167	  // bundle still yields a per-month rate; then price the customer's chosen term
168	  // through the SAME formula VPS uses. For a monthly game server this is exactly
169	  // `priceCents`; an ANNUAL game server renews at 12× that, less the annual discount.
170	  const gameMonthlyCents = isGame
171	    ? Math.round((grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents) / Math.max(1, server.gamePlan!.termMonths))
172	    : 0;
173	  // LEGACY GUARD. Game servers sold BEFORE terms existed carry no frozen annual rate
174	  // (`annualDiscountPct == null`) and always renewed at the plan's FLAT `priceCents`,
175	  // with no term discount ever applied. Preserve that exactly so no pre-existing game
176	  // server's renewal moves — only servers sold through the new term-aware flow (which
177	  // always stamps a frozen `annualDiscountPct`) are priced with `termPriceCents`.
178	  //
179	  // GUARD ON isGame FIRST. This value is only USED in the isGame branch below, but a
180	  // bare ternary evaluates it for EVERY server — and a VPS `PricedServer` (e.g. the one
181	  // the deploy wizard builds, `gamePlan: null`, no `annualDiscountPct`) then hits the
182	  // `annualDiscountPct == null` arm and dereferences `server.gamePlan!.priceCents` on a
183	  // null, crashing the whole deploy page with "Cannot read properties of null". Compute
184	  // 0 for non-game so the null is never touched.
185	  const gameTotalCents = !isGame
186	    ? 0
187	    : server.annualDiscountPct == null
188	      ? (grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents)
189	      : termPriceCents(gameMonthlyCents, months, annualPct);
190	  // Bill the IP surcharge only when the server BOTH actually holds a dedicated
191	  // IP AND the customer chose/paid for it (`wantsDedicatedIp`). Requiring
192	  // `dedicatedIp` alone used to mean two very different bugs at different times:
193	  // a NAT-fallback server (paid for an IP, pool was empty, never got one) being
194	  // charged for an IP it never received, and — found 2026-09-15 via a real
195	  // customer's admin profile showing a $2.99 "committed MRR" they never agreed
196	  // to — the opposite case: a VPS granted a dedicated IP for FREE by the
197	  // `dedicated_ip_default` platform setting (see worker/index.ts's provision())
198	  // being silently billed for it anyway on the next renewal. Requiring BOTH
199	  // flags fixes both directions: no charge without the address, no charge
200	  // without genuine customer intent to pay for it.
201	  const dedicatedIpBillable = !!server.dedicatedIp && server.wantsDedicatedIp;
202	  const netCents = isGame
203	    ? gameTotalCents + (dedicatedIpBillable ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0)
204	    : vpsTermPriceCents(grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.plan.priceCents, months, annualPct) +
205	      (dedicatedIpBillable ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0) +
206	      extraDiskCents +
207	      backupCents;
208	  // VAT/GST on the pre-tax subtotal. Default rate 0 keeps `totalCents === netCents`
209	  // for every caller that does not pass the owner's rate (Finding 1).
210	  const taxRatePercent =
211	    Number.isFinite(prices.taxRatePercent) && (prices.taxRatePercent ?? 0) > 0 ? prices.taxRatePercent! : 0;
212	  const taxCents = Math.round((netCents * taxRatePercent) / 100);
213	  return {
214	    months,
215	    netCents,
216	    taxCents,
217	    taxRatePercent,
218	    totalCents: netCents + taxCents,
219	    extraDiskCents,
220	    extraDiskMonthlyCents,
221	    backupCents,
222	    backupMonthlyCents,
223	    label: isGame ? server.gamePlan!.name : `${server.plan.name} VPS`,
224	  };
225	}
226

705:model Server {
706-  id                    String              @id @default(cuid())
707-  uptimeDays            ServerUptimeDaily[]
708-  name                  String
709-  label                 String? // customer-facing nickname (rename)
710-  // Set when this order arrived via a partner deep link (?ref=kodely on
711-  // /dashboard/deploy, captured by PartnerSourceCapture). Null for every direct
712-  // Nxeon order. Gates the webhook notify in worker/index.ts on provision success.
713-  partnerSource         String?
714-  hostname              String
715-  vmid                  Int?                @unique
716-  status                ServerStatus        @default(PENDING)
717-  ipAddress             String?             @unique
718-  sshPort               Int?                @unique
719-  rootPassword          String?
720-  rootPasswordEnc       String?
721-  isFree                Boolean             @default(false)
722-  autoRenew             Boolean             @default(true)
723-  gameVariant           String? // game-server type/loader (e.g. paper, carbon, bepinex) — see lib/game-config
724-  gameConfig            Json? // per-game settings values (validated against the family schema)
725-  // Minecraft-only: `<subdomain>.play.nxeon.cloud`, resolved via a per-server DNS
726-  // SRV record (worker/game-subdomain.ts) instead of the free tier's shared
727-  // mc-router — see lib/game-subdomain.ts for the shared name-validation rules.
728-  // Null until the customer sets one; unique across THIS column only — cross-
729-  // checked against FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain at the application layer since
730-  // Postgres can't enforce a unique constraint across two different tables.
731-  subdomain             String?             @unique
732-  suspendedNote         String?
733-  // WHY a server is suspended: "UNPAID" | "ABUSE" | "ADMIN". Null = never suspended.
734-  //
735-  // `suspendedNote` used to be the only signal, and nothing consumed it, so every
736-  // suspension looked identical to the billing engine. Two live consequences:
737-  // (1) `terminateOverdue` selected on `status: "SUSPENDED"` alone, while the
738-  //     renewal sweep EXCLUDES suspended servers — so an admin suspending a
739-  //     paid-up customer pending an investigation meant they were never charged,
740-  //     never warned, their term lapsed, and 13 days later their VM and all its
741-  //     data were destroyed with a "prolonged non-payment" notice they had never
742-  //     been given a chance to act on.
743-  // (2) `renewNow` auto-unsuspended ANY suspended server on payment, so a spammer
744-  //     suspended for outbound abuse could pay and put themselves straight back
745-  //     on the network.
746-  // Both now scope strictly to UNPAID.
747-  suspendReason         String?
748-  // Human-readable reason a PROVISION failed terminally, set by the worker on the
749-  // ERROR path (worker/index.ts). Surfaced on the server detail page's ERROR
750-  // banner so the customer sees WHAT went wrong instead of a bare red status dot.
751-  // Cleared when a retry re-enqueues provisioning. Null = never failed (or the
752-  // failure predates this column).
753-  provisionError        String?
754-  // Best-effort, human-readable label for whichever real provisioning phase is
755-  // running RIGHT NOW (e.g. "Cloning your server…", "Waiting for the game server
756-  // to start…") — written by worker/index.ts's provision() between real,
757-  // observable checkpoints (clone / config / start / guest-agent boot / SSH
758-  // reachable / game port open). Read by lib/provisioning-step.ts and shown by
759-  // <ProvisioningOverlay/> in place of its cosmetic time-based cycling text.
760-  // Null = no real signal available yet (falls back to the cosmetic text) or the
761-  // server isn't mid-provision. Never cleared explicitly — it's simply ignored
762-  // once status leaves PENDING/PROVISIONING.
763-  provisioningStep      String?
764-  expiresAt             DateTime?
765-  // ---- Dunning (failed auto-charge retry state) ----
--
1503:model Coupon {
1504-  id             String             @id @default(cuid())
1505-  code           String             @unique
1506-  kind           CouponKind
1507-  value          Int
1508-  scope          CouponScope        @default(ANY)
1509-  // Which product family this coupon may be used on at checkout. ANY = no
1510-  // restriction; VPS / GAME limit it to that kind of order.
1511-  serviceKind    CouponServiceKind  @default(ANY)
1512-  // Restrict to ONE specific plan by slug (e.g. "starter"). Null = any plan
1513-  // within `serviceKind`. This is how "one free month on the Starter VPS" is
1514-  // locked to Starter and cannot be spent on a bigger plan.
1515-  planSlug       String?
1516-  // Cap how many months of the term the coupon may discount. 1 = one month only,
1517-  // so a percentage/free coupon cannot be stretched across a 12-month order to
1518-  // give a year free. Null = the whole term.
1519-  maxTermMonths  Int?
1520-  firstTimeOnly  Boolean            @default(false)
1521-  minAmountCents Int?
1522-  maxRedemptions Int?
1523-  timesRedeemed  Int                @default(0)
1524-  expiresAt      DateTime?
1525-  active         Boolean            @default(true)
1526-  note           String?
1527-  createdAt      DateTime           @default(now())
1528-  redemptions    CouponRedemption[]
1529-}
1530-
1531:model CouponRedemption {
1532-  id               String    @id @default(cuid())
1533-  couponId         String
1534-  coupon           Coupon    @relation(fields: [couponId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
1535-  userId           String
1536-  user             User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
1537-  amountCents      Int       @default(0)
1538-  context          String    @default("")
1539-  // Hashed claimant IP (sha256 of ip+salt) — enforces "once per person" beyond
1540-  // one-per-account, so a coupon can't be farmed with throwaway signups. Null on
1541-  // legacy rows / when the IP was unavailable; Postgres treats NULLs as distinct
1542-  // so the unique below never collides on them.
1543-  ipHash           String?
1544-  // Reservation lifecycle — the fix for the card/Stripe (up-front-settlement) race,
1545-  // mirroring PromoRedemption below. UNLIKE the promo, a coupon carries a CONFIGURABLE
1546-  // cap (`Coupon.timesRedeemed` / `maxRedemptions`) on top of the two unique slots, so
1547-  // the reserve/release helpers (lib/coupon-redemption.ts) increment/decrement that
1548-  // counter in lockstep with a hold's creation/deletion.
1549-  //   CONSUMED — a GRANTED redemption. The wallet-atomic path (lib/order.ts
1550-  //              claimOrderCoupon) inserts this directly, so the default keeps that
1551-  //              insert-and-grant flow behaving exactly as before.
1552-  //   RESERVED — a HOLD taken at checkout-CREATE time, BEFORE the card is charged, so a
1553-  //              second concurrent card checkout can't also pass the per-person/global
1554-  //              caps and walk away discounted. Confirmed to CONSUMED at fulfilment, or
1555-  //              released (row deleted + timesRedeemed decremented) on expiry/sweep.
1556-  // Both states occupy the same (couponId,userId)/(couponId,ipHash) unique slots, so a
1557-  // live hold blocks a second claim exactly like a grant does.
1558-  state            String    @default("CONSUMED")
1559-  // When a RESERVED hold may be reaped if never confirmed. Set to the Checkout session's
1560-  // payable lifetime plus a grace buffer, so a payment landing at the last instant still
1561-  // confirms. Null for CONSUMED grants.
1562-  reservedUntil    DateTime?
1563-  // Opaque token tying a RESERVED hold to its Checkout session (carried through the card
1564-  // round-trip in Stripe metadata as `nxeonCouponReservation`). Unique so confirm/release
1565-  // target exactly one row and a replayed create can't double-hold. Null for CONSUMED rows.
1566-  reservationToken String?   @unique
1567-  createdAt        DateTime  @default(now())
1568-
1569-  @@unique([couponId, userId])
1570-  @@unique([couponId, ipHash])
1571-  @@index([state, reservedUntil])
1572-}
1573-
1574-// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
1575-// Managed promotions — the sitewide "first month free" offer.
1576-// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
1577-// One row per successful redemption of a managed promo. Today there is exactly
1578-// one promo (`promoId = "first-month-free"`), but the shape is promo-keyed so a
1579-// second offer never needs a schema change.
1580-//
1581-// The two @@unique constraints ARE the caps (owner decision, fixed at 1/account
1582-// + 1/IP): a conditional INSERT that violates either one is how a second
1583-// redemption is refused atomically inside the order's charge transaction — the
1584-// exact mechanism CouponRedemption uses. `ipHash` is nullable and Postgres
1585-// treats NULLs as distinct, so the per-IP unique never collides on a missing IP
1586-// (card-settle path / IP unavailable); the per-account unique still holds.
1587-//
1588-// The free-month credit is applied to an order ONLY when the matching row here
1589-// was successfully inserted. If the insert loses a race (already redeemed by
1590-// this account OR this IP) or the promo is switched off, the order is charged
1591-// the FULL price instead — it never fails, it just doesn't get the credit.

Since account deletion already requires zero active servers, the retention offer for Feature 2 mainly needs to trigger on the cancelService flow rather than deletion itself, which simplifies things.

So actually the real hook is cancelService in period_end mode — that's the case where a future renewal still exists that a discount could apply to. Immediate termination destroys the server outright with a refund, so there's nothing left to discount there. If the customer accepts the retention offer, autoRenew stays on and pendingRenewalDiscountPercent gets set to 50 to apply at the next billing cycle.

For account deletion specifically, since it already requires zero active servers, there's no live server left to attach a discount to at that point — the flow just blocks deletion and tells the user to cancel servers first, so the retention interstitial doesn't really have a natural place to live there.

Given time constraints, I'll implement the retention modal to intercept both the "cancel auto-renewal" action and the "immediate termination" action, since those are the points where there's an actual server eligible for a discount. 27	 * ----------------------------------------
28	 * Every numeric field on this page is a free-text box that an operator types into
29	 * once, at speed, usually during an incident — and several of them multiply money

32	 * while the panel showed 0%, and the auto-suspend kill switch reported "Saved." and
33	 * then let the sweep take customer VMs offline anyway. Both were silent.
34	 *
35	 * So values are validated HERE, at the write, and an out-of-range entry is REFUSED
36	 * with a message naming the allowed range rather than quietly stored or quietly

5	 * the admin create path (`adminCreateCoupon`) writes, so all of the checkout

11	 *   kind/value      PERCENT 50  → 50% off
12	 *   scope           ORDER       → redeemed at service checkout (not wallet top-up)
13	 *   serviceKind     VPS         → the product family the checkout coupon flow
14	 *                                 evaluates (orderQuote scopes orders as VPS).
15	 *                                 NB: shared-hosting checkout does not yet consume
16	 *                                 coupons, so VPS is the honest working scope.
17	 *   maxTermMonths   1           → discount only the first term/month, so a 12-month
18	 *                                 order can't stretch 50% across a whole year
19	 *   maxRedemptions  500         → sane global cap
20	 *   1 per user/IP               → enforced automatically by the unique
21	 *                                 (coupon,user) + (coupon,ipHash) redemption rows
22	 *   active          true

 * customers only). Claimed the SAME way typing a promo code by hand already
 * is: `couponCode` on the order, validated/applied through
 * lib/order.ts/lib/coupon-order.ts's normal checkout-coupon path.
 *   code            EXIT25
 *   kind/value      PERCENT 25  -> 25% off
 *   scope           ANY         -> not locked to top-up vs order; the actual
 *                                  gate is `firstTimeOnly` + the wizard only
 *                                  ever sends it on a VPS/game order
 *   serviceKind     ANY         -> works on either VPS or game (the popup
 *                                  shows on both pricing steps)
 *   maxTermMonths   1           -> first term/month only, so a 12/24/36-month
 *                                  order can't stretch 25% across the whole
 *                                  commitment
 *   firstTimeOnly   true        -> the whole point of the popup
 *   maxRedemptions  null        -> uncapped; firstTimeOnly + the per-user/IP
 *                                  CouponRedemption uniques already prevent
 *                                  abuse, and this discount is meant to run
 *                                  indefinitely for every new customer
 *   active          true
 *
 * STAY50 — cancel-plan retention offer. NOT applied through the checkout
 * coupon-stacking path at all (there is no new order for it to apply to) —
 * claiming it (lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts claimRetentionOffer) only uses
 * this row for the real coupon engine's atomic one-per-account claim
 * (the conditional `timesRedeemed` increment + the `@@unique([couponId,
 * userId])` on CouponRedemption); the actual 50%-off DISCOUNT is applied at
 * renewal time through `Server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent` (see
 * lib/renewal-charge.ts). Its `scope`/`serviceKind`/`planSlug`/`maxTermMonths`
 * are therefore inert for this coupon — set to the same harmless defaults an
 * admin-created ANY/ANY coupon would get.
 *   code            STAY50
 *   kind/value      PERCENT 50  -> 50% off (informational; renewalCharge does
 *                                  not read Coupon.value — RETENTION_DISCOUNT_
 *                                  PERCENT in lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts
 *                                  is the actual number that gets applied, and
 *                                  is kept in sync with this by convention)
 *   scope           ANY
 *   maxRedemptions  null        -> uncapped globally; the per-account cap (one
 *                                  offer per customer, ever) is the
 *                                  CouponRedemption unique, not this field
 *   firstTimeOnly   false       -> this is an EXISTING customer's offer
 *   active          true
 *
 * Run:  npx tsx scripts/seed-discount-coupons.ts
 */
import { db } from "../lib/db";

async function upsertCoupon(code: string, data: Parameters<typeof db.coupon.create>[0]["data"]) {
  const coupon = await db.coupon.upsert({
    where: { code },
    update: data,
    create: { code, ...data },
  });
  console.log(
    `✔ ${code} ready: ${coupon.value}% off (${coupon.scope}/${coupon.serviceKind}), ` +
      `firstTimeOnly=${coupon.firstTimeOnly}, maxTermMonths=${coupon.maxTermMonths ?? "—"}, ` +
      `maxRedemptions=${coupon.maxRedemptions ?? "unlimited"}, active=${coupon.active}, ` +
      `redeemed ${coupon.timesRedeemed}.`,
  );
}

async function main() {
  await upsertCoupon("EXIT25", {
    kind: "PERCENT",
    value: 25,
    scope: "ANY",
    serviceKind: "ANY",
    planSlug: null,
    maxTermMonths: 1,
    firstTimeOnly: true,
    minAmountCents: null,
    maxRedemptions: null,
    expiresAt: null,
    active: true,
    note: "Exit-intent popup — 25% off the first term for first-time customers, deploy wizard pricing step.",
  });

  await upsertCoupon("STAY50", {
    kind: "PERCENT",
    value: 50,
    scope: "ANY",
    serviceKind: "ANY",
    planSlug: null,
    maxTermMonths: null,
    firstTimeOnly: false,
    minAmountCents: null,
    maxRedemptions: null,
    expiresAt: null,
    active: true,
    note: "Cancel-plan retention offer — 50% off the next renewal only, claimed via lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts claimRetentionOffer (NOT the checkout coupon path). One redemption per account, ever, enforced by the CouponRedemption unique constraint.",
  });
}

main()
  .then(() => process.exit(0))
  .catch((e) => {
    console.error("Failed to seed discount coupons:", e);
    process.exit(1);
  });

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
# comment on this same step for the 2026-09-10 incident). Its output does NOT
# include public/ or .next/static/ (Next's documented behavior) — refresh
# them every promote, same as staging, or new/changed static assets are
# missing from prod until the next promote happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle since it reads .dat files off its own package path at runtime) — the
# standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace as JS-imported, so
# an externalized package's own non-JS data files are silently left behind.
# Found live 2026-09-10 on staging: this crashes EVERY request with an
# uncaught ENOENT the moment something runs the standalone server.js instead
# of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around geoip.lookup() does NOT
# help, the failure isn't confined to that call. Copy the real data/
# directory every promote, same reasoning as public/.next/static above. This
# has NOT yet bitten production because nxeon-web's systemd unit still runs
# `npm start` (next start) today, not server.js directly — but this fix must
# land before that switch happens, not after.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi
# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. .next needs to be writable by it
# (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable. .env is the one
# exception: systemd's EnvironmentFile= reads it as root (PID 1, pre-privilege
# drop) so the app's process env is fine either way, but Prisma's generated
# client ALSO opens .env directly at Client instantiation to resolve its own
# env() directives — that read happens as the actual 'nxeon' process user, so
# a root-owned .env throws EACCES there on every cold start (harmless once
# systemd's injected vars are already in process.env, but noisy, and a prior
# root-run edit to this file silently reverted the ownership fix below once
# already — confirmed live 2026-09-02). Keep .env nxeon-owned, not world- or
# group-readable. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next/.env ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chown nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "==> Restarting production web"
systemctl restart nxeon-web

# Drain in-flight provisions before bouncing the worker. Restarting the worker
# mid-provision used to interrupt a live VM build and (with a non-idempotent retry)
# strand the server in ERROR. The start step is now idempotent so this is
# belt-and-suspenders, but avoiding the interruption entirely is cleaner. Bounded
# wait (max ~4 min) so a deploy can never hang forever.
DBURL=$(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon/.env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
if [ -n "$DBURL" ] && command -v psql >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for _ in $(seq 1 24); do
    ACTIVE=$(psql "$DBURL" -tAc "SELECT count(*) FROM \"Job\" WHERE status='RUNNING' AND type='PROVISION';" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ "${ACTIVE:-0}" = "0" ] && break
    echo "==> Waiting for ${ACTIVE} in-flight provision(s) to finish before restarting worker…"
    sleep 10
  done
fi

echo "==> Restarting production worker"
systemctl restart nxeon-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1/)
echo "==> Production responds: HTTP $CODE"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "PRODUCTION UNHEALTHY — check journalctl -u nxeon-web"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Production promote complete"

### 2026-09-19 — Two discount features: exit-intent popup (25%) + cancel-plan retention offer (50%)

Both reuse the REAL coupon engine for eligibility/one-time bookkeeping rather than inventing a
parallel discount mechanism, but apply it through two different code paths because the two triggers
are fundamentally different — one is a checkout-time discount on a new order, the other has to land
on a FUTURE RENEWAL CHARGE against an EXISTING server, where there is no new order for the checkout
coupon-stacking logic to fire on at all.

**Exit-intent popup (EXIT25, 25% off, first-time customers only).** Shown once per visit on the
deploy wizard's pricing step (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`'s `Wizard`, both VPS "Choose your plan"
and game "Size your server" — both keyed `"configure"` in `components/nx/order.tsx`) when the mouse
leaves the viewport toward the browser chrome (`document.mouseleave`, `clientY <= 0` — no exit-intent
detection existed anywhere in this codebase before this). Gated server-side (never a client-only
check): `isFirstTimeCustomer` (zero non-free `Server` rows — the same predicate `firstTimeOnly`
coupon enforcement already uses in `lib/order.ts`/`lib/coupon-redemption.ts`) is resolved in
`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` and threaded down as a prop, alongside the `exit_intent_enabled`
admin setting. "Claim now" does not settle a price itself — it autofills the wizard's own
`couponCode` state with `EXIT25` and lets the existing quote effect (`components/nx/order.tsx`)
validate/apply it through the exact path typing the code in by hand already uses; a toast confirms
the fill while the Payment step's own coupon-label UI is the real confirmation once the quote
round-trips. New: `components/nx/ExitIntentModal.tsx`. Shown-once state is a plain `useState` in
`Wizard`, not localStorage — a per-visit nudge, not a claim record; the real one-time enforcement is
server-side (`firstTimeOnly` + the per-account/per-IP `CouponRedemption` uniques already enforced by
`claimOrderCoupon`).

**Cancel-plan retention offer (STAY50, 50% off the very next renewal only).** Shown as an
interstitial the instant a customer clicks either cancel path in `components/customer/
CancelService.tsx` (turn off auto-renew / terminate immediately), before `cancelService` itself runs.
Accepting it (`claimRetentionOffer`, new in `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`) does NOT cancel
anything — it claims STAY50 (one redemption per ACCOUNT, ever, via the real
`@@unique([couponId, userId])` `CouponRedemption` constraint — ​cancelling a *different* server later
does not offer it again, a deliberate choice to prevent farming one 50%-off per server) and stamps
`Server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent = 50` (new nullable Int column) onto that one server.
`renewalCharge()` (`lib/renewal-charge.ts`) reads the field and shaves that percent off the WHOLE
renewal subtotal (plan + every add-on line) for exactly that one renewal, before tax, exposing the
shaved amount as `retentionDiscountCents` so the invoice can show it as its own line (mirroring how
extra-disk/backup already get their own lines). The field is cleared back to `null` in the SAME
compare-and-swap transaction that actually commits the renewal — `worker/billing.ts`'s
`commitRenewal` (the automatic sweep, and everything that funnels through it: wallet, saved-card, and
PayPal renewals) and `lib/actions.ts`'s `renewNow` (the manual "Renew now" button) both clear it
unconditionally on a successful advance, so it can never silently reapply to the period after. New:
`components/customer/RetentionOfferModal.tsx` (accept = stays + discount pending; decline = the
original cancellation proceeds exactly as before — a real choice, not a dark pattern).
`retentionOfferEligible` (also new in `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`) is resolved server-side in
`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` and threaded into `CancelService` as a prop, gated on the
`retention_offer_enabled` admin setting, the server having a real billing term, no discount already
pending, and the account never having redeemed STAY50 before.

**Both** get an admin on/off toggle (`exit_intent_enabled` / `retention_offer_enabled`, both default
TRUE) following the exact `WinbackPanel`/`lib/actions-settings.ts` shape — new panels
`ExitIntentPanel.tsx` / `RetentionOfferPanel.tsx`, new settings-page tabs "Exit-intent popup" /
"Retention offer". Both real `Coupon` rows (code `EXIT25`: PERCENT 25, `firstTimeOnly` true,
`maxTermMonths` 1, uncapped `maxRedemptions`; code `STAY50`: PERCENT 50, `firstTimeOnly` false,
uncapped `maxRedemptions` — the per-account cap is the `CouponRedemption` unique, not this field) are
seeded/refreshed idempotently by `scripts/seed-discount-coupons.ts` (`npx tsx
scripts/seed-discount-coupons.ts`, modeled on `scripts/seed-launch-coupon.ts`) — run once per
environment (staging, then production) before either feature can actually apply a discount.

New automated tests: `test/retention-offer.test.ts` — pure-arithmetic proof that the 50% discount
halves the very next renewal (whole subtotal, before tax), proof it does not apply once
`pendingRenewalDiscountPercent` is cleared, and source-code assertions (same style as
`test/money-core-guards.test.ts`) that both `commitRenewal` and `renewNow` clear the field inside
their own compare-and-swap write, and that `claimRetentionOffer`/`hasRetentionOfferAvailable` refuse
a second claim per account. 11/11 passing; full suite run alongside shows the same pre-existing,
unrelated failures present on `main` before this change (confirmed by diffing failing-test names
against a `git stash`-baseline run) — no new failures introduced.

Entry points: `prisma/schema.prisma` (`Server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent`); `lib/renewal-charge.ts`
(`PricedServer.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent`, `RenewalCharge.retentionDiscountCents`);
`lib/renewal-quote.ts`; `worker/billing.ts` (`commitRenewal`); `lib/actions.ts` (`renewNow`);
`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts` (`claimRetentionOffer`, `retentionOfferEligible`,
`hasRetentionOfferAvailable`); `components/customer/{CancelService,RetentionOfferModal}.tsx`;
`components/nx/{DeployView,ExitIntentModal}.tsx`; `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`;
`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`; `lib/settings.ts`; `lib/actions-settings.ts`;
`components/admin/settings/{ExitIntentPanel,RetentionOfferPanel}.tsx`; `app/admin/settings/page.tsx`;
`scripts/seed-discount-coupons.ts`; `test/retention-offer.test.ts`.
